theme_zh: 找房子、看房子：問清楚租屋條件
summary_zh: 學會用現在完成進行式說「最近一直在…」，並在看房時問清楚房租、水電、押金和租約，也能跟同事朋友聊找房子的近況。

vocab.definition: a legal agreement that lets you rent a home for a fixed period
vocab.example: My lease ends in March, so I need to decide whether to renew it.
vocab.example_zh: 我的租約三月到期，所以要決定要不要續約。

vocab.definition: money you pay a landlord before moving in, which you get back if you don't damage anything
vocab.example: The security deposit is two months' rent.

vocab.definition: services such as electricity, water and gas, or the bills you pay for them
vocab.example: The rent is reasonable, but utilities aren't included.
vocab.example_zh: 房租還算合理，但不含水電瓦斯。

vocab.definition: one problem that is serious enough to make you say no to something
vocab.example: Not having a washing machine isn't a deal-breaker for me, but not having an elevator is.
vocab.example_zh: 沒有洗衣機我還能接受，但沒有電梯就不行。

vocab.definition: something that is much cheaper than you would expect
vocab.example: At that price, a two-bedroom near the MRT is a steal.
vocab.example_zh: 捷運站附近的兩房只要這個價錢，根本是撿到便宜。

vocab.definition: already containing furniture such as a bed, sofa and table
vocab.example: I'd prefer a furnished place, so I don't have to buy a bed.
vocab.example_zh: 我比較想找附家具的房子，這樣就不用買床。

vocab.definition: to pay part of the money for something so that it is kept for you
vocab.example: If you like the place, you can put down a deposit today.
vocab.example_zh: 如果你喜歡這間，今天就可以先付訂金。

vocab.definition: to watch carefully so that you notice something when it appears
vocab.example: Can you keep an eye out for apartments near your office?
vocab.example_zh: 你可以幫我留意你公司附近的房子嗎？

reading.title: Three Months of Apartment Hunting: What I've Learned
paragraphs: I've been looking for a new apartment since August, and I'm starting to think I could write a guide. I've been swamped at work, so most of my searching has happened late at night on my phone, scrolling through listings that look perfect in photos and slightly less perfect in real life.

The first thing I've learned is to read the whole listing. A rent that looks like a steal often doesn't include utilities, and in summer the air conditioner alone can add a surprising amount to your monthly bill. I now ask every landlord the same question before I even book a viewing: "What's included in the rent?"

Second, know your deal-breakers. For me, it's a long commute and no natural light. I've been tempted a few times by big, cheap places in the suburbs, but I know I'd hate spending two hours a day on the train. A smaller, furnished studio closer to the office suits me much better.

Third, be ready to move fast. Good apartments in my area disappear within days. Last month I found a lovely place near a park, but by the time I'd asked a coworker to cover for me so I could leave early and see it, someone else had already put down a deposit. Now I always have enough money set aside for a security deposit, which is usually two months' rent here.

Finally, read the lease carefully before you sign. Check how long it is, whether you can leave early, and who pays for repairs. My friends have been teasing me about how picky I am, but I'd rather wait a little longer than sign a year-long lease for the wrong place. I'm still keeping an eye out for the right one, and I'm feeling hopeful.

questions.q: Why has the writer done most of the searching late at night?
options: Landlords post new listings at night
The writer has been very busy at work
Viewings are only available in the evening
The writer prefers to search on a computer
questions.explain_zh: 第一段：「I've been swamped at work, so most of my searching has happened late at night」——工作太忙，只能晚上找。

options: A small studio and no furniture
High utilities and a short lease
A long commute and no natural light
Living near a park and a noisy street
questions.explain_zh: 第三段：「For me, it's a long commute and no natural light.」

questions.q: Why does the writer now have money set aside for a security deposit?
options: Because landlords no longer accept late payments
Because the writer lost a good apartment by not acting quickly enough
Because the deposit in the area has recently doubled
Because the writer's friends told them to
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：第四段說上個月看中的房子，等作者請同事幫忙頂一下、提早離開去看時，已經被別人付了訂金。所以現在先把押金準備好，下次才能馬上決定。

grammar.point: Present perfect continuous for ongoing situations
grammar.point_zh: 現在完成進行式：描述「從過去一直持續到現在」的狀況
grammar.explain_zh: have/has been + V-ing 用來說一件從過去開始、到現在還在進行（或剛停但看得到影響）的事，常和 for／since／lately／recently 一起用：I've been looking for an apartment since August.（從八月找到現在，還在找）。對照組：I've seen three apartments this week. 用現在完成式，強調「次數／結果」；I saw an apartment yesterday. 有明確過去時間點，用過去式。know、like、own 這類狀態動詞通常不用進行式：I've known my landlord for years.

examples.en: I've been looking for an apartment since August.
examples.zh: 我從八月就一直在找房子。

examples.en: We've been talking about moving for months, but we haven't decided yet.
examples.zh: 我們討論搬家已經好幾個月了，但還沒決定。

examples.en: You're out of breath. Have you been carrying boxes up the stairs?
examples.zh: 你喘成這樣，是不是一直在搬箱子上樓？

exercises.q: She ___ (look) for a new place for three months, and she still hasn't found one.
exercises.explain_zh: for three months 而且到現在還沒找到，用 has been + V-ing；主詞 She 用 has。

exercises.q: "How long ___ in this apartment?" — "About two years. I really like it here."
options: are you living
have you been living
did you live
do you live
exercises.explain_zh: How long 問「從過去到現在」持續多久，而且現在還住在這裡，用 have you been living。

options: I've been knowing my landlord for years.
I've known my landlord for years.
I'm knowing my landlord for years.
I know my landlord since years.
exercises.explain_zh: know 是狀態動詞，不用進行式；持續到現在用現在完成式 have known + for。

exercises.q: I ___ three apartments this week, but none of them felt right.
options: have been viewing
have viewed
am viewing
view
exercises.explain_zh: 有明確「數量」（three apartments）時，強調結果，用現在完成式 have viewed；進行式強調的是「一直在做」的過程，不和次數搭配。

exercises.q: The neighbors ___ (make) noise since 7 a.m. I can't even sleep in on a Saturday!
exercises.explain_zh: since 7 a.m. 一直吵到現在，用 have been + V-ing；主詞 The neighbors 是複數，用 have。

listening.title: Apartment news at the office

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Jenny
lines.text: You look tired, Kevin. Have you been working late again?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Kevin
lines.text: Not exactly. I've been staying up looking at apartment listings. My lease ends next month.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Jenny
lines.text: Oh no, that's stressful. Have you found anything you like?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Kevin
lines.text: I saw a furnished one-bedroom yesterday. It's close to the MRT, and honestly, the rent is a steal.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Jenny
lines.text: So what's the catch?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Kevin
lines.text: Utilities aren't included, and the landlord wants a two-month security deposit plus the first month's rent up front.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Jenny
lines.text: So that's three months' rent all at once? That's a lot. Is that a deal-breaker for you?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Kevin
lines.text: Not really. I've been saving up for this, so I can manage it. I just want to read the lease carefully first.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Jenny
lines.text: Good idea. If you need to go see it again during work hours, I can cover for you.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Kevin

questions.q: Why has Kevin been staying up late?
options: He has been working on a big project
He has been looking at apartment listings
He has been moving boxes into his new place
He has been talking to his landlord
questions.explain_zh: Kevin 說：「I've been staying up looking at apartment listings.」

questions.q: What is the downside of the apartment Kevin saw?
options: It's far from the MRT
It doesn't come with furniture
Utilities aren't included and he has to pay a lot up front
The lease is too short
questions.explain_zh: Kevin 說：「Utilities aren't included, and the landlord wants a two-month security deposit plus the first month's rent up front.」——不含水電，而且一開始就要先付一大筆錢。

questions.q: How does Kevin seem to feel about the apartment overall?
options: He likes it and will probably take it
He thinks it's too expensive
He wants Jenny to see it first
He has decided to keep looking
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：他說押金不是 deal-breaker、自己有存錢，還說「I'll probably put down the deposit this weekend」，可見他滿喜歡、很可能會租。

prompts.question: A friend asks, "So, what have you been up to lately?" Tell them about two things you've been doing recently.
prompts.question_zh: 朋友問你：「最近都在忙什麼？」說說你最近一直在做的兩件事。

prompts.question: You're viewing an apartment. Ask the landlord three questions before you decide.
prompts.question_zh: 你正在看房子，決定之前問房東三個問題。
hints: How much is the security deposit?
prompts.sample: I really like the place. Are utilities included in the rent, or do I pay them separately? How long is the lease, and can I leave early if I need to? And how much is the security deposit?

writing.task: You've been looking for an apartment and found one you like. Write a short message to the landlord: say how long you've been looking, ask about the utilities, the lease and the security deposit, and suggest a time to view it again.
writing.task_zh: 你找房子找了一陣子，終於看到喜歡的一間。寫一則簡短訊息給房東：說你找了多久、詢問水電費、租約和押金，並約一個時間再去看一次。
writing.sample: Hi Mr. Chen, my name is Amy, and I saw your apartment on Minsheng Road last Saturday. I've been looking for a place near my office for about two months, and yours is the best one I've seen so far. Before I decide, could I ask a few questions? Are utilities included in the rent, or are they paid separately? How long is the lease, and is it possible to leave early? Also, how much is the security deposit? If possible, I'd like to view the apartment again this Thursday after 7 p.m. Thank you, and I look forward to hearing from you. Best regards, Amy

清楚問到水電費、租約、押金
語氣禮貌，開頭自我介紹、結尾道謝

reading.title: Why Some Renters Keep Losing Out
paragraphs: Anyone who has been apartment hunting in a big city lately knows the feeling: you spot a listing that checks all the boxes, message the landlord within the hour, and are told it's already gone. It's tempting to blame bad luck, but agents say the renters who keep losing out tend to make the same handful of mistakes.

The most common one is hesitation. Many people like to sleep on a decision, which is sensible when you're buying a car but costly in a market where decent places are snapped up in days. Agents suggest doing the thinking before the viewing, not after it: know your budget, your non-negotiables and the neighborhoods you'd genuinely consider, so that when the right place turns up, you can commit on the spot.

The second mistake is showing up empty-handed. Landlords who have been fielding dozens of inquiries are understandably drawn to tenants who make their lives easy. Someone who arrives with proof of income and a reference from a previous landlord sends a clear signal: I'm organized, and I'll pay on time. In a tight market, that can matter more than offering a little extra rent.

Finally, there's the opposite problem: being so eager that you skim the fine print. A rent that seems too good to be true sometimes comes with strings attached, such as a clause allowing the landlord to raise the rent after six months, or one making the tenant responsible for every repair. Reading the lease line by line is tedious, but it beats discovering those surprises after you've moved in.
None of this guarantees success, of course. But renters who prepare tend to spend weeks, not months, searching, and they're far less likely to end up somewhere they regret.

questions.q: Why do agents say that sleeping on a decision can be costly?
options: Because rents go up every night
Because good apartments are often taken before you decide
Because landlords dislike tenants who ask questions
Because it makes renters choose the wrong neighborhood
questions.explain_zh: 第二段說好房子「are snapped up in days」，所以考慮一晚再決定，房子可能就被租走了。

questions.q: What does the writer suggest about offering extra rent?
options: It is the best way to win an apartment
Landlords usually refuse it
It may matter less than showing you are a reliable tenant
It is only useful in small cities
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：第三段說帶收入證明和推薦信、讓房東覺得你可靠，「can matter more than offering a little extra rent」。

questions.q: Which of these is given as an example of "strings attached"?
options: A landlord who asks for a reference
A clause that lets the landlord raise the rent after six months
A tenant who brings proof of income
A viewing that is booked within the hour
questions.explain_zh: 第四段：「such as a clause allowing the landlord to raise the rent after six months」。

listening.title: To renew or not to renew

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Sophie
lines.text: So, did you hear back from the landlord about renewing?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Daniel
lines.text: Yeah, and — brace yourself — he wants to raise the rent by fifteen percent.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Sophie
lines.text: Fifteen? You're kidding. We've been here three years and we've never paid late once!

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Daniel
lines.text: I know. I've been going back and forth on it all morning. Part of me says we should just pack up and—

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Sophie
lines.text: —and spend every weekend for two months looking at overpriced places? No thanks.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Daniel
lines.text: Okay, fair. But we can't just swallow a fifteen percent increase, either.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Sophie
lines.text: Why don't we try negotiating? Like, offer to sign a two-year lease if he meets us halfway.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Daniel
lines.text: Hmm. That could actually work. Landlords hate having to find new tenants.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Sophie
lines.text: Exactly. And we've been taking really good care of the place — remember when we fixed that leak ourselves?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Daniel
lines.text: Right, we should definitely mention that. I'll call him tonight.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Sophie
lines.text: Maybe email him instead? That way we have everything in writing.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Daniel
lines.text: Good point. I'll draft something and send it to you before it goes out.

questions.q: Why is Sophie surprised by the rent increase?
options: The landlord promised never to raise the rent
They have been good tenants for three years
The apartment is in poor condition
Daniel already agreed to it
questions.explain_zh: Sophie 說：「We've been here three years and we've never paid late once!」住了三年從沒遲繳，覺得不該漲這麼多。

options: Moving to a smaller studio
Accepting the increase without complaining
Offering to sign a longer lease in exchange for a smaller increase
Asking the landlord to fix the leak
questions.explain_zh: 她說：「offer to sign a two-year lease if he meets us halfway」——用簽兩年約換取房東各退一步。

questions.q: Why does Sophie prefer email to a phone call?
options: She wants a written record of what is agreed
The landlord never answers his phone
Daniel is bad at negotiating on the phone
Email is faster than calling
questions.explain_zh: 她說「That way we have everything in writing.」——留下書面紀錄，之後才不會有爭議。
